# The report and the record

## What every report holds

Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.

A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.

A fact is a finding that is an established property of the tree, the language, the library or their tools, and that later work builds on. A defect also gets its ledger row, and a fact about it may cite the row.

A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.

Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:

- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
- **For FACTS.** Each fact that your work established, in the hand-over form of "Writing to the record". If your brief let you write FACTS, give instead the number of each entry that you added or rewrote. If your work established no fact, write "none".
- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.

## At a point to report

- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
- Then finish the work.
- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.

## Timings and citations

- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.

## POSITIONS and FACTS

POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.

Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".

## The gap ledger

The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.

- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.

Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.

A row states its gap as it stands now. A note adds a fact. If your work changes what a row says, write the row's whole new line with `rewrite` (below), not a note that tells the repair.

The heading reader of `ledger.py` does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:

    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh

- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.

A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.

Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:

    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE

## Writing to the record

- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`, never by hand. `add` gives a new entry its number, and `set` rewrites an entry. The tool writes the entry to `FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md`, and its earlier text to the history file beside it. It commits nothing: commit both files in one commit. Its header gives its usage.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, add each fact as a new entry in the section of its topic, in the commit that establishes it. Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers. Point the entry to that section, by your report's file and the section's heading. If your report is only your final message, hand the fact over instead. Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work.
- If your brief does not let you write FACTS, hand each fact over in the "For FACTS" item of your report, with:
  - the fact as it stands now, in one sentence;
  - what it means for the work;
  - the number that a decision rests on, if any, with what it counts; if its parts belong to different ledger rows, the part of each row;
  - the test that fails if the fact stops holding, or the command and the output that show it;
  - the section of your report that holds the detail.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, rewrite a wrong entry in place. Otherwise say in your hand-over that the entry is wrong, with the evidence.
- POSITIONS holds each of the curator's decisions, in one place. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.

Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.

    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

To add a row:

1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

To change a row:

- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N. It refuses a note that takes the row past 1,200 characters, or its notes cell past 700 characters. `$L note N TEXT --check` writes nothing. It says whether TEXT fits, and how many characters the notes and the row have left now and would have left with TEXT. These counts include the separator that the tool adds. It exits 0 if TEXT fits, and 1 if not. Run it before a long note, or before a note on a row near its limits. If TEXT does not fit, shorten it, or cut the notes with `rewrite` (below).
- `$L rewrite N FILE` replaces row N with the whole line in FILE, a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with N or `?` in its number cell. Use it to correct the claim, cut the notes or change the reproducer. The tool checks the line against the template and keeps the old line in the history file.
- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it. NAME can also be a file under `explorations/coordinator/tools/`, or `none` with `--note REASON`. For a `CONTESTED` row, add `--settled TEXT`, which names what settled its question.
- `$L landing-check BASE` prints each problem, and exits 1 on any. Run it when your brief asks for it. It checks the whole ledger against the template, so a broken row that BASE already had counts too. The problems are a row that breaks the template, an `XXX` test deleted or renamed while a row that is not closed names it, a row that is not closed though a commit says it fixed it, and a FACTS or POSITIONS entry that disagrees with a row's status.

## The repository's history

- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.
- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's. After the tag `sealed-tree`, commit `75cca6683`, the revival began to fix the team's code, test first. Before it, the revival changed mainly the build and the toolchain.
- `git diff a874948ac -- FILE` shows what the revival changed in a file, and `git diff 75cca6683 -- FILE` what it changed after the tag.
- If the commands above fail, run `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`. It prints `true` in a shallow clone, where these commits do not resolve. There, a copyright header of Sun Microsystems or Oracle, as in `Library/Format.fss`, marks a file that the team made, but not which of its lines the port or the revival changed. If your task needs those lines, say in your report that the clone is shallow.
- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a `git log` of a directory stops at a cut and misses the team's earlier commits. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.
- Commit `8fe1daa8f` copied a third-party port of the tree to Java 9 onto the team's last commit, `a874948ac`. Give its lines no credit, and name no author of it in any text that you commit. In a reconstruction of authorship, attribute nothing of it to anyone.

# Analysis: process engineering and post-mortems

Process engineering measures what the work costs and how long it takes, and tests a change to the process. A post-mortem finds out what happened and why.

## Measuring

- Each batch's spend by stage is in `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-29/characterization.md`, and by role in `process-engineering/README.md` beside it. Each batch record holds its own.
- Read a run's spend with `spend.py` (the core, "tokens written").
- Estimate a boot from the files' sizes: a read costs one token per 2.5 to 3 bytes. `/context` shows what the last call held.
- To compare a Fable token's share of the session limit with an Opus token's, ask the curator to read the usage panel over a window with Fable workers and over one with Opus alone.
- If an iteration of the work waits long on something, find the cause and fix it.
- Keep a test of a process change small, and run it on the records at hand. Design no elaborate evaluation.
- If you compare two workflows, compare what each run found, not only what it cost. Check first that the batch represents the workload: the specification, the checker, the interpreter and the library.

## Finding out what happened

- Send archaeology to Sonnet scouts (`references/delegating.md`).
- The transcripts are on the `transcripts-blinded` branch. `cloud-container`'s loss part says how to read another session's transcript.
- `explorations/coordinator/tools/journal-text.py` copies a field of an agent's result from a Workflow journal.
- In a post-mortem, give an index into the transcript by timestamp, with a script that prints any verbatim view. Never restate the transcript.
- Build the profile of what the curator knows as a task of its own, by archaeology, in a file of its own.

Load the `fortress-repo` skill first. You work in `/home/user/fortress`, on `main`.

## The problem

`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` is the project's list of established facts, one entry per line under a permanent number such as `F-87`. Rules have asked since October 2026 that an entry stays near 600 characters, that detail needed only while doing the work (line numbers, lists of sites, lists of tests, timings) stays in the report that the entry points to, and that how a fact came about (dates, batches, corrections, repairs) goes to `FACTS-history.md`.

- 352K at its earlier peak, `720db2671`, 2026-09-30;
- 90K after a consolidation, `b67abe3d2`, 2026-10-13 20:13 UTC;
- 140K on 10-20, 245K on 10-27, 278K on 11-03, 329K on 11-10, 387K on 11-17;
- 428K at `9de4c69bc8`, 2026-11-24, with 339 entries, 299 of them over 600 characters.

`INDEX.md` grew over the same time from about 200K to 392K.

The curator, the person in charge, has ordered an archaeology: the rules and the checks were in place, so what went wrong? Your part is one slice of the evidence. An Opus writer will read your file with four others and write the report.

## What you return

- Evidence only: exact words, numbers and their sources. Cite each item by its commit hash, its file and line, or its transcript file and timestamp.
- No judgement of who or what is at fault, no cause that the evidence does not state, no proposal of a fix, no recommendation. Where two sources disagree, give both.

- Your final message: the file's path and five lines on what it holds. Not the evidence again.

- Write only your own output file. Do not edit or commit anything else. - Bound every command's output (`head`, `cut -c`, `wc`). Never print a transcript or a whole record file.
- Keep every wait under 240 s.

- Each record-landing run's files: `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-<N>/record-landing/`, for climb batches 25 to 35b.
- The October consolidation and the rule's design: `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/facts-slice-1.md` to `facts-slice-7.md`, `record-rule-draft.md`, `record-test/`, `record-store-design.md`, `record-store-review.md`, `record-landing-workflow.md`, `record-landing-replay-24.md`, `record-origins-evidence.md`.

- The curator is named Pavol in the record. Write "the curator". The coordinating session is "the coordinator".

input.prompt:
You write one report for the Fortress revival's curator, the person in charge. Load the `fortress-repo` skill first, then read `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md` whole (the rules that the report examines) and `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/analysis.md`, "Finding out what happened". You work in `/home/user/fortress`, on `main`.

## The problem

`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` holds the project's established facts, one entry per line under a permanent number. Rules ask that an entry stays near 600 characters, that detail needed only while doing the work stays in the report that the entry points to, and that how a fact came about goes to `FACTS-history.md`. The file was 352K characters on 2026-09-30, 90K after a consolidation on 2026-10-13 (`b67abe3d2`), and 428K on 2026-11-24 (`9de4c69bc8`), with 339 entries, 299 of them over 600 characters. A boot of the coordinating session that reads the record whole now costs about 590K tokens of context.

On 2026-11-24 the coordinating session ("the coordinator") proposed a cleanup to the curator as if the growth were new. He rejected it. His words, at 07:35 UTC, cleaned of dictation errors:

"You are treating this as a new problem. It is reoccurrence of the old problem. ... You will perform archaeology because there were already rules in place ... You are saying that test lists, sites and line numbers go to the reports, and dates and repairs go to the history. You are saying this shit is landing in the facts. Like, we already had processes that were supposed to deal with this. We need to analyze what the fuck went wrong."

## Your task

Answer his question from the evidence: which rules and checks were in place to keep FACTS lean, what put the text into the entries all the same, and why each rule or check did not stop it.

Five scouts gathered the evidence this morning. Read all five files whole before you write:

- `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/evidence/growth-by-source.md`: which commits grew FACTS, by how much and of which kind; new entries against grown entries; the 40 largest.
- `.../evidence/rules-text-history.md`: the exact words of each rule and check on an entry's form and length, and how they changed.
- `.../evidence/guards-in-action.md`: what each check did in the sixteen record-landing runs, the judge's rulings, ten applied growths, and what was done with the reports of entries over 600.
- `.../evidence/words-and-prior-alarms.md`: the curator's words, the earlier occurrences from 2026-09-24 on, each later measurement or alarm, and what the coordinator wrote about the cause.
- `.../evidence/entry-anatomy.md`: what the characters of the entries are made of at the two commits, with 24 entries side by side.

The scouts were Sonnet workers who returned evidence without judgement. Take their files as evidence to weigh, not as conclusions. Where a claim carries the report's argument, check it at its source with a bounded command (`git show`, `git log -S`, `grep -n`, a short Python script over `git show COMMIT:PATH`): a number that two files give differently, a quoted rule, a count of what a check did. Say in the report which claims you checked and which you took from a scout's file. Where the evidence does not reach, say so; do not fill the gap.

## What the report holds

Write `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/REPORT.md`, with a first line `<!-- ... -->` that says in one sentence what it is, for whom, when and from what.

1. **The answer in short**, first: at most 1,500 characters, plain sentences that a person can take in on a phone screen, with the few numbers that carry it. It says what went wrong, in the order of how much each cause explains.
2. **The occurrences.** Each time the record grew and was cut, or its size was raised, from September to today: the date, the size, what was decided, and what rule or tool changed afterwards. Short.
3. **What the growth is.** How much came from which kind of commit; how much is new entries at their birth size against growth after birth; what the added characters are (lists of tests, pointers to detail, citations by file and line, sentences on ledger rows, repairs and changes, the rest), in characters and shares.
4. **Each rule and each check, one by one.** For each: its words, with file and commit; who or what applies it; what its text says happens when an entry is over 600 characters or holds detail or provenance; what it did in fact, in counts; and why it did not stop the growth, as far as the evidence shows. Include the rules that themselves ask an entry to hold more (the parts that an entry must hold; what a landing makes an entry "owe"), if the evidence shows that they added characters. Include what the coordinator did with each report of entries over 600, stated plainly, with no softening and no defence.
5. **What the curator said and decided about the record's size**, by date, in his exact words where they are the decision, and what became of each decision in the rules.
6. **What the evidence does not show.** The gaps, and the questions it leaves open.

Mark each cause as shown by the evidence, or as your inference from it. Give the evidence for each by the scout file's name and its section heading, so that a reader can print the passage; do not copy long passages.

## Limits and form

- **No fix, no recommendation, no proposal, no "next steps".** The curator reads the findings first and decides what follows. A sentence that says what should change does not belong in this report.
- The whole report: at most 16K characters. The detail stays in the five evidence files.
- Write halfway to ASD-STE100: plain short sentences, active voice, one word for one thing. Define each term of the tooling where you first use it, in a few words (for example, the record-landing workflow: the workflow that brings the record in line with a batch after it lands; its judge; `lengths.py`; an owed clause; the pass; a rung). Use lists; use a table only for numbers. Write numbers as K where the exact value does not matter. No metaphor, no closing summary line.
- Write "the curator" and "the coordinator", never "you" or a name. The curator's quoted words stay exact.
- Give each time in UTC with its date, taken from the evidence, never from feel.
- Write only `REPORT.md`. Do not edit or commit anything else, and do not commit `REPORT.md`: the coordinator commits it. Write none of `FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md`, their histories, `INDEX.md`, `PLAN.md`, `review-queue.md` or the gap ledger: another run is writing them now, so read the record's states with `git show COMMIT:PATH`, the present one at `9de4c69bc8`.
- Do not build or run any Fortress command. Bound every command's output. Keep every wait under 240 s.

Your final message: the report's path, its section "The answer in short" copied whole, the claims that you checked at their source, and each place where two evidence files disagree.

## 4. Each rule and each check

Terms. A **rung** is one worker's part of a climb batch: code, tests, and draft entries. The **gather** folds the drafts into FACTS. The **commit stage** writes the gate's figures. **The pass** rewrites drafts into the record's form (`record.md`, "The pass"). The **record-landing workflow** brings the record in line with a batch after it lands, from climb batch 25: a sorter lists each change owed, a writer writes it, a checker checks it, an Opus judge applies or holds it. An **owed clause** is the text that a listed change needs. **`lengths.py`** prints each changed entry's length and names each entry already over 600 that grew.

**(a) The 600 measure.** "Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence." (`record.md:31`; first at `7b434aae52`, 10-13 19:22; checked). Applied by: not named. In fact: entries over 600, 38 to 299. Why: no one is named to act on it, and it lets a long entry stay. The draft's budget, "a chunk's total stays under 600 characters times its entries", never reached `record.md`; "Name that reason in the pass's report" was cut 24 minutes after the first text (`f6bc1aa753`). (shown: rules-text-history.md, "1b", "1c")

**(b) The six questions.** Question 3 sends "a date, a batch, a correction" to the history; question 4 keeps "a line number, a list of sites, a timing" in the report. Applied by: a writer who reads `record.md`. In fact: see section 3. Why: the batch script quotes no question (checked), so rung workers and the gather never see them. The landing writer does, but its judge checks growth only. (shown)

**(c) What an entry holds.** "The test that gates it" and "the report section that holds the detail"; since 10-22 (`b6f5268e1d`, `6becc28f95`) also the conditions, the kind of evidence, and the decision "by number and subject" (`record.md:18`, checked). The landing brief adds the commit that bounds a measurement, and the landing's figures for a claim it extends (`entries.md:36-37`, checked). These parts match classes that grew: tests +28K, "Detail:" +23K, pointers to entries +50K. The rule names one test and one report section; entries now hold up to 19 test names and 12 report paths. Clauses that name a worker's or planner's choice: none at `b67abe3d2`, 17 clauses, 2.4K, at `9de4c69bc8` (this report's count). (words shown; lists inferred)

**(d) The workers' rule.** "Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers." And: "Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work." (`fortress-repo` `records.md:82`, checked, no number; since `8ca0d7e615`, 10-13). In fact: births at a median of 1,192, 165 of 182 over 600. Why: it leaves the length to the pass (item f). (shown)

**(e) The batch script.** Rung brief: "its evidence (the file:line, the command with its output, the test) ... Completeness is yours; the record pass owns the final wording", the entry "in a few lines" (`climb-batch-workflow.js:623`). Gather: "in a few lines" (`:1045`). Commit stage: "0 failures" (`:1622`). No 600 for an entry, and no quote of "The pass" (checked). Why: the brief asks for file and line, and no batch stage cuts the draft. (shown: rules-text-history.md, "5")

**(f) The pass.** "In a batch, the commit stage runs it, with this part quoted in its prompt. After a lone worker, you run it." Step 5: "Report each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its extra sentence." (`record.md:73`, `:84`; checked). No reader is named. Why: the script never received it; the passes by hand cut little. (shown: guards-in-action.md, "4")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# final.sh RUN: the record-landing workflow's last step, which its judge runs after it writes final.apply,
# final.rewrite (if a row changes), diff.md, commit-1.txt and commit-2.txt in the run's folder RUN.
#
# Runs checks.sh RUN final: the six record files reset to AT, final.apply and final.rewrite applied, the new
# rows of final.add (or, without it, rows.add) added with ledger.py add, and every check again. If a check fails, it commits nothing and exits 1: the judge holds the change that fails
# and runs this again. If all pass, it makes two commits on the run's branch in the worktree, each by named
# paths, each message from its file, then the line "By the climb batch N landing workflow (Opus).", which
# names the tier of the agents that wrote the text, then the footer of the fortress-repo skill's committing part:
#   1. FACTS.md, POSITIONS.md, their histories, the gap ledger and its history, where they changed;
#   2. every other changed file under explorations/ (PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX, other
#      notes) and the run's folder, its *.log files left out (git ignores them; the rounds' .done markers
#      are in the worktree's tmp/record-landing/, which git ignores too).
# The judge writes nothing after this script commits, so the worktree stays clean; it prints any file left.
# A changed file outside explorations/, the boot note or the held list (the coordinator's), or a new file
# outside the run's folder, stops it before any commit. Once the branch holds commits past AT, it prints
# them and does nothing more, so a resumed run commits nothing twice. It pushes nothing.
set -uo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
RUN=${1:?usage: final.sh RUN}
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$RUN/run.env"
made=$(git -C "$WT" log --format='%h %s' "$AT..HEAD")
if [ -n "$made" ]; then
  echo "final.sh: the branch $BRANCH holds its commits already:"; echo "$made"; exit 0
fi
for f in diff.md commit-1.txt commit-2.txt; do
  [ -s "$RUN/$f" ] || { echo "final.sh: write $RUN/$f first" >&2; exit 1; }
done
"$here/checks.sh" "$RUN" final || { echo "final.sh: a check fails ($RUN/mech-final.md); hold the change that fails it, and run final.sh again"; exit 1; }

lines: +<!-- Post-mortem of FACTS's regrowth from 90K to 427K characters (2026-10-13 to 2026-11-24): the rules and checks in place, what put the text into the entries, and why none stopped it; for the curator, written 2026-11-24 from the five scouts' files in evidence/ and checks at source. -->
+# FACTS regrew: what went wrong

+Dates are 2026, times UTC. Sizes are characters. "Shown": the evidence shows it. "Inference": this report concludes it. A source (file, "heading") is a scout's file in `evidence/`. "Checked": checked here at its source.
+## 1. The answer in short

+FACTS grew from 90K characters on 10-13 to 427K on 11-24. The rules on length were in place the whole time. No rule on length was enforced: the checks print lists, the one hold covers only growth, and no stage had the job of cutting.
+What put the text in:

+- Rung commits, whose workers' draft entries stayed at the length written: 58% of the growth. New entries came in at a median of 1.2K, 165 of 182 over 600. Workers are told to spend no effort on wording, since a later pass rewrites it. No batch stage ran that pass. From 11-03 the record-landing workflow ran it: 342 entry rewrites in 16 runs added 5K and brought 2 entries net under 600. (shown)
+- The clarity rewrite of 10-22: 25%. The curator accepted that growth as the cost of clarity. Nothing trimmed it later. (shown)
+- The coordinator's own filings: 15%. (shown)
+Why nothing stopped it:

+- The landing judge holds only an entry already over 600 that grows by more than its owed clause. It let 140 of 155 such growths through. A new long entry, or one that stays long, passes every check. (shown)

+- `record.py` and `lengths.py` list the long entries and exit 0. At its own record writes the coordinator saw the list grow from 228 to 285, and acted on none. Reviews of 11 batches named long entries and left them to the coordinator, who ran no consolidation. (shown)
+- The coordinator knew on 11-02 that the drafts were not cut, and first named the count to the curator on 11-24. (shown, checked)
+## 2. The occurrences
+- **09-27.** Boot rose from about 125K to 245K tokens. The curator refused a FACTS target under 25K. Decided: no size target; FACTS consolidated before each batch (P-130).
+- **09-30.** FACTS peaked at 352K (08:00, `720db2671`); a consolidation at the curator's order ended the day at 309K (checked).

+- **10-02.** Cause found: rung entries, about 14 KB a batch. The curator chose "option 2": a rung's entry "in a few lines, a few hundred bytes", cut by the gather if longer (`6a9661477e`). 65 entries shortened; 309K to 228K.
+- **10-08.** The batch redesign removed "a few hundred bytes" and the cut (`e020159857`, checked).

+- **10-13.** Seven slices took FACTS from 302K to 258K, median unchanged. The record rule's consolidation then cut it from 257.6K to 90.2K (`b67abe3d2`, 20:13). Rule: "near 600 characters", "a check, not a cap".
+- **10-22.** The clarity workflow: 140K to 223K; entries over 600 from about 85 to 161.
+- **11-02.** The record-landing workflow replaced "before each batch launches" (`5114bfeceb`, checked); its judge holds growth past 600 (`575d555945`).
+- **11-16.** Light-boot post-mortem: FACTS 95K to 363K bytes. Decided: a light boot. No size rule changed.
+- **11-23.** Process review: 290K to 403K bytes; "No rule sets a size at which the inflow stops." No rule changed.
+- **11-24.** Full boot 590K tokens. FACTS 427K, 339 entries, 299 over 600, median 1,198 (checked). A cleanup, proposed as new, rejected at 07:35.
+Sources: (words-and-prior-alarms.md, "Timeline"); (rules-text-history.md, "0", "8").
+## 3. What the growth is
+FACTS grew by 337,199 characters. By kind of commit (growth-by-source.md, "Totals per kind"; clarity and landing checked):
+| kind | commits | net | share |
+| rung commits: code, tests, draft entries | 128 | +194K | 58% |
+| clarity workflow, 10-22 | 5 | +83K | 25% |
+| coordinator's edits and filings | 57 | +49K | 15% |
+| review folds and repairs | 31 | +7K | 2% |
+| record-landing runs | 16 | +5K | 2% |
+| consolidation | 1 | −2K | −1% |
+By entry (same file, "3. New entries against grown entries"; checked):
+| part | characters | share |
+| 182 new entries, at birth | 220K | 65% |
+| the same entries, growth after birth | 40K | 12% |
+| 157 older entries, growth | 77K | 23% |
+Rung commits wrote 129 of the births (169K), the coordinator's edits 41 (38K), the clarity workflow 11 (12K). The clarity workflow added 62K of the older entries' 77K.
+What the added characters are. Each sentence counts once, in the first class whose marker it holds (entry-anatomy.md, "1. The parts, by script"):
+| class | added | share |
+| list of tests | +28K | 8% |
+| "Detail:" pointer to a report | +23K | 7% |
+| cites code by file and line | +41K | 12% |
+| names a ledger row | +48K | 14% |
+| points to another entry | +50K | 15% |
+| commit hash, date, batch or rung | +9K | 3% |
+| a repair or change word | +4K | 1% |
+| bold title | +39K | 12% |
+| the rest | +91K | 27% |
+| prefixes, spaces, other lines | +3K | 1% |

+The classes are markers, not judgements. Entries that cite file and line: 8 to 126; that hold a date, batch or rung: 90 to 267; a commit hash: 2 to 28. Test names per entry: median 1 to 2, largest 3 to 19 (same file, "2."). Of the 1,324 "rewritten" blocks in `FACTS-history.md`, 198 re-anchor line citations that a landing moved (this report's regex count).
+## 4. Each rule and each check

+Terms. A **rung** is one worker's part of a climb batch: code, tests, and draft entries. The **gather** folds the drafts into FACTS. The **commit stage** writes the gate's figures. **The pass** rewrites drafts into the record's form (`record.md`, "The pass"). The **record-landing workflow** brings the record in line with a batch after it lands, from climb batch 25: a sorter lists each change owed, a writer writes it, a checker checks it, an Opus judge applies or holds it. An **owed clause** is the text that a listed change needs. **`lengths.py`** prints each changed entry's length and names each entry already over 600 that grew.

+**(a) The 600 measure.** "Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence." (`record.md:31`; first at `7b434aae52`, 10-13 19:22; checked). Applied by: not named. In fact: entries over 600, 38 to 299. Why: no one is named to act on it, and it lets a long entry stay. The draft's budget, "a chunk's total stays under 600 characters times its entries", never reached `record.md`; "Name that reason in the pass's report" was cut 24 minutes after the first text (`f6bc1aa753`). (shown: rules-text-history.md, "1b", "1c")

+**(b) The six questions.** Question 3 sends "a date, a batch, a correction" to the history; question 4 keeps "a line number, a list of sites, a timing" in the report. Applied by: a writer who reads `record.md`. In fact: see section 3. Why: the batch script quotes no question (checked), so rung workers and the gather never see them. The landing writer does, but its judge checks growth only. (shown)

+**(c) What an entry holds.** "The test that gates it" and "the report section that holds the detail"; since 10-22 (`b6f5268e1d`, `6becc28f95`) also the conditions, the kind of evidence, and the decision "by number and subject" (`record.md:18`, checked). The landing brief adds the commit that bounds a measurement, and the landing's figures for a claim it extends (`entries.md:36-37`, checked). These parts match classes that grew: tests +28K, "Detail:" +23K, pointers to entries +50K. The rule names one test and one report section; entries now hold up to 19 test names and 12 report paths. Clauses that name a worker's or planner's choice: none at `b67abe3d2`, 17 clauses, 2.4K, at `9de4c69bc8` (this report's count). (words shown; lists inferred)

+**(d) The workers' rule.** "Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers." And: "Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work." (`fortress-repo` `records.md:82`, checked, no number; since `8ca0d7e615`, 10-13). In fact: births at a median of 1,192, 165 of 182 over 600. Why: it leaves the length to the pass (item f). (shown)

+**(e) The batch script.** Rung brief: "its evidence (the file:line, the command with its output, the test) ... Completeness is yours; the record pass owns the final wording", the entry "in a few lines" (`climb-batch-workflow.js:623`). Gather: "in a few lines" (`:1045`). Commit stage: "0 failures" (`:1622`). No 600 for an entry, and no quote of "The pass" (checked). Why: the brief asks for file and line, and no batch stage cuts the draft. (shown: rules-text-history.md, "5")

+**(f) The pass.** "In a batch, the commit stage runs it, with this part quoted in its prompt. After a lone worker, you run it." Step 5: "Report each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its extra sentence." (`record.md:73`, `:84`; checked). No reader is named. In fact, 10-14 to 11-02: the commit stage never ran it. By hand, one pass after batch 14 cut 6K (`15a6d4365`); after batch 24 a record writer cut 3 of 17 long entries and left 11 untouched. Why: the script never received it; the passes by hand cut little. (shown: guards-in-action.md, "4")

+**(g) "Run it on FACTS before each batch launches."** (P-130, 09-27; `record.md` from 10-13; checked). In fact: from 10-13 to 11-02 the commits that cut FACTS total 14K, against 193K added (this report's count); one is labelled a consolidation (`bd33a2f8b`, −2K). Replaced 11-02. (shown)

+**(h) `record.py check`.** `SIZE = 600  # ...; reported, never refused`. It lists the long entries under "reported, not failing" and does not fail on them (`record.py:126`, `:1198-1201`, `:1303`; checked). No write command tests length (rules-text-history.md, "4"). In fact: it printed 228 long FACTS entries on 11-08, 252 on 11-16, 285 on 11-23. Why: it never refuses, and no one acted on the list. (shown: guards-in-action.md, "5")

+**(i) The record-landing workflow.** Sorter: every entry the batch added or changed gets "the pass" (`sort.md:40`). Writer: "An entry already past 600 characters grows only by the clause that its change owes" (`entries.md:38`). Checker: a sentence past 600 stays with a named question (`check.md:27`). `lengths.py`: "Information only; exit 0". Judge: "Hold an entry already past 600 characters that grows, unless the clause that its change owes alone explains the growth" (`judge.md:24`). All checked. In fact, in 16 runs:
+- 342 FACTS entry rewrites; FACTS +5K net; entries over 600 down by 2 net (guards-in-action.md, "1. The sixteen runs").
+- `lengths.py` named 155 grown entries; the judge applied 140, held 15 (checked), 14 of them for length.
+- No held text landed later. Held entries grew by other routes: F-405 1,613 to 2,307, F-333 1,445 to 1,759 (same file, "The held changes").
+- The sorter named 47 changes "past 600 characters", against 343 of "the pass". Of the 43 FACTS entries so named, 27 shrank, by 3.7K in all; 9 grew; 7 stayed (this report's count).

+Why: the hold covers only growth of an entry already long; nothing asks a new or long entry to shrink. The owed clause is itself new text, so most growth passes by the rule's own terms (inference). The workflow "takes no pilot", though its design note says "Only the curator's read of a small pilot caught length, register, history in an entry and the wrong home" (`record-landing-workflow.md:76`, checked). (shown)

+**(j) The clarity writer.** "Keep each entry near 600 characters as a check, not a cap. Clarity comes first." (`record-clarity/writer.md:36`). Its judge judges meaning only. In fact: +83K on 10-22. Why: the brief puts clarity first, and the curator accepted the growth. (shown: rules-text-history.md, "7")
+**(k) The reports, and what the coordinator did with each.**
+- `record.py`'s list at its own writes, 11-08 to 11-23: no step on length (guards-in-action.md, "5").
+- Workers' hand-backs: "All 11 are over 600 characters" (11-08), "Every new entry is over 600 characters" (11-13). No step on length.
+- The judges' "each by its owed clause", 16 runs: each run landed as judged. Of the 15 held changes, it rewrote four entries of batch 26 by hand 34 minutes later, with other texts (`7ecb207b0`).

+- Reviews of batches 17 to 25 and the batch records named long entries, some with "Home: the coordinator's consolidation" (checked). It ran no such consolidation. All 30 entries so named are still over 600; 25 are as long or longer than on 11-03 (F-252 2,086 to 4,330).

+- 11-02 00:09, to the curator: "all 17 entries that batch 24 added or changed stand over the record's 600-character check, and the writer trimmed six" (checked). It then proposed the record-landing workflow, whose checks hold only growth.
+- From 11-07 to 11-24 07:05 its chat named no count of long entries (checked). At 07:05 it put the growth to the curator as a new problem.
+## 5. What the curator said and decided about the record's size

+- **09-27 02:21** (checked): "I found your target of FACTS under 25k too aggressive." 05:52: "consolidation of facts skills happen before starts of batches, as workers read these and pay the cost". Became: P-130, then `record.md`'s "before each batch launches"; replaced 11-02.
+- **09-29 21:27** (checked): "the target token count is, is not the important thing. Important thing is the fidelity of the record." Became: no size target in any rule.
+- **10-02 10:52** (checked): "FACTS option 2 now. Before we launch batch 8." Became: "a few hundred bytes"; gone from the script 10-08.

+- **10-12 11:23**, on recording dates and provenance: "What collapses, like it doesn't scale"; "there should be some post processing. Pass by the coordinator." Became: the history files and the pass.

+- **10-13 17:23** (checked): "I really hope that the consolidated record is significantly smaller than before. Like that is a goal." At 15:38, in the coordinator's rendering only: "600 or 1,000, an entry needs a reason to be large". Became: the 600 check; its stated reason cut that evening (item a).

+- **10-22 08:19** (checked): "I think that's just the cost we are willing to pay for Clarity." And: "The process needs to be encoded in the skill ... If the record starts drifting again." Became: the clarity tool; no rule says when the record drifts.
+- **10-28 07:37** (checked; on POSITIONS): "We already invented this process. ... We have probably failed to encode how to use it correctly next time."
+- **11-02**: yes to the record-landing workflow's eight defaults. Became: the workflow, with no pilot.
+- **11-07 05:54**: "landing should trigger full load of POSITIONS and FACTS". **11-16 22:47**: a light boot, FACTS searched. Became: boot rules; no size rule.

+- **11-24 07:03** (checked): "Full boot is now 590k of your context. ... We should probably run some garbage collection on FACT". 07:35 (checked): "Regarding your proposal on splitting the index and trimming the facts, reject it."
+Source: (words-and-prior-alarms.md, "1", "3A", "4").
+## 6. What the evidence does not show
+- Why the 600 and the pass never reached the batch script on 10-13; why "a few hundred bytes" left it on 10-08; why the reason clause and the chunk budget were dropped. No commit message says.
+- Whether the 140 applied growths were truly owed. Only the judges' words support it.
+- Whether shorter entries keep decisions as good: the record test ran on 10-13 only.
+- What "the rest", +91K, holds. The classes are regex markers.
+- Why the sorter named only 47 "past 600" changes while 204 to 295 entries stood over 600.
+- Whether the curator approved that `record.py` never refuses for size. His words on it were not found.
+- The coordinator's chat before 11-07 was searched here with one pattern, not read.
+Claims marked "checked" or "this report's count" were checked at source; all else is from the scouts' files as cited.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer

content.content:
## The landing

The landing check is `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, run by the gather and by the merged-diff review on the batch's base. It reports a row that breaks the template, an `XXX` test removed while a row that is not closed names it, a row that is not closed though a commit says it fixed it, and a FACTS or POSITIONS entry that disagrees with a row's status. A finding the base already had counts too. The gather clears each finding before its commit, through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or by a reworded entry. The merged-diff review clears any that is left in its corrections commit. So a batch lands only when the check prints nothing.

The batch workflow holds the push when a point to report still acts against a decision on record after the repairs. Its result then gives `pushHeld` true, and `heldBy` lists the points. If the batch's push is held for the curator, take steps 1 to 3 at once on the local commits. Only these wait: the push, the parts of step 3's routing check that need the pushed hashes, and step 4, since the record-landing workflow pushes `main` itself. If `heldBy` names either of these, push only after the curator's go:

- a step that cannot be undone;
- a change that still acts against the curator's word.

For every other held push, this paragraph is the standing go. If the last line of step 3's review names no change, push the batch yourself, by `fortress-repo`'s committing part. If the line names a change, put it to the curator as a hold, and push only after the curator's go. The review's commit of step 3 goes with that push. Then run step 4.

1. Sweep the batch agents' to-dos from the session's shared task list: `explorations/coordinator/tools/sweep-tasks.py --delete`. If another workflow still runs, add `--running`, which removes only the completed tasks. The agents write these to-dos themselves, and the harness shows the whole list to every agent.
2. Name each decision that landed in one line.
3. Have one Opus reviewer, which only reads, check the landed changes against the decisions on record and the library's way; measure misses by kind, the briefing's use and cost, and re-measuring; and run the routing check (the manual, "After the landing: the coordinator's routing"). If the batch's push is held, have the reviewer end its review with one line. The line names each landed change that must not reach `main`, or says that there is none. Have the review's section on cost count the tokens written in three spans, each on its own. Give the reviewer each span as two times, read from the commits and the workflow journals:

   - the landing work of the batch before: from its commit stage's last commit to the end of its record-landing workflow;
   - the preparation: from then to the launch of the batch under review;
   - the run: from that launch to its commit stage's last commit, which stands also while the push is held.

   Have the reviewer count a span as `spend.py` from its start less `spend.py` from its end, over the same folders. A transcript then counts in the span where it last changed.
4. After the post-batch review is committed, run the record-landing workflow (`explorations/coordinator/tools/record-landing/README.md`). It brings FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX, PLAN and the review queue in line with the landing. Its Land stage, the step that lands its commits on `main`, also pushes them. Then it runs the orientation workflow in update mode itself, on the entries that the landing added or changed. The orientation workflow writes new text for each section of `fortress-repo`'s `revival-changes.md` that these entries touch. Next, the workflow has the skill writer install the sections that the orientation judge accepts. The writer also brings in line the sentences of `fortress-repo`'s `SKILL.md` and other parts that the landing's changes to FACTS and POSITIONS made false, and no others. A new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, is not made in the workflow: the writer lists it for you in its reports, `writer-1.md` and `writer-2.md` in `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/skills/`. After the workflow ends, judge each such rule on its merits: what it protects against what it costs, its ground, and whether the skill already covers it. Then take it or drop it. Give the rules that you take to your own skill writer. They land after their cold read and the writer's fixes (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"). Name the rules that you dropped, with their reasons, in one line of the message that sends the curator the one line for the page of `fortress-repo` changes (below). The workflow runs a cold read of the writer's changes, and the writer fixes its flags. Then it has a worker update the page of `fortress-repo` changes (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7), and pushes the writer's commits, as its Land stage pushes the record's. Last, if every push went through, it updates the revival page with `update.py`, commits and pushes the files that the script names, and republishes the page. No step of yours comes between. Its result gives one line: the commits and the link of the page of `fortress-repo` changes (the README, "The skill update"), then the revival page's commit and version (the README, "The revival page"). If the landing made no sentence of the skill false and the orientation judge did not run, no writer starts, and the line names only the revival page. While the workflow runs, start no skill-writer task of your own on `fortress-repo`.

   Then read the workflow's commits on `main`, as the README's "Landing its result" says. If the result's `stopped` is set, take the step that the README gives for it there, or, for the revival page, in "The revival page": a stopped push leaves the commits on the local `main`, for you to push or take off. If a page's agent could not publish, the line names that page's files and URL: publish them yourself by that URL. Decide each held section of the orientation update, in its `queue.md`, as any decision: only a consequential one goes in the review queue. Ask whether you would have done anything differently. Tell the curator of its POSITIONS changes as `SKILL.md`, "Quiet times", says. Send the curator the one line for the page of `fortress-repo` changes (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions") when "Quiet times" allows: while the curator is away, hold it with the reports of skill changes. Once the reviews show the workflow sound, stop this review, and rely on what the workflow does.

content.content:
Last, only when the Push stage pushed everything, the workflow keeps the revival page current (`../revival-page/README.md`), as the coordinator did by hand after climb batch 26's landing (`0868faa51`). No step of the coordinator's comes between.

1. **The script.** A Sonnet agent runs, in the main tree, `python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/revival-page/update.py --landing N --run-start base` in the background and waits in steps of 230 s. The run start is the script's documented proxy, the time of the base commit that the gather record names, and the new `landings.csv` row's note says so: the run start that the other rows hold, the first line of the batch run's first agent, is only in its transcripts, and the tree holds no other time of the launch (the gate summary's `# machine --- gate batch N` time is the gate's start). For the eight batches from climb batch 20 to 26 whose gather record names its base, the base commit's time is the row's run start, or up to three minutes before it. If the script stops (exit 2: a source's form changed), the run stops there, landed and pushed, and `stopped` gives the script's message; nothing of the page is committed.
2. **The commit and the push.** The same agent commits the paths that the script prints in its first step, and the five data files that its note names, by named paths, with the message that it prints, "By the climb batch N landing workflow." and the committing part's footer, as `folders.sh` commits; then it pushes as the Push stage does, when `git log origin/main..main` lists only that commit.
3. **The republish.** A Sonnet agent (`revival-publish.md`) reads the page's URL, `PAGE_URL` in `update.py`, and the artifact's published `record-growth.png`, and publishes `revival-story.html` with `record-growth.png` as its supporting file by that URL. If it cannot publish, the result's `line` names the two files and the URL, for the coordinator to publish by it.

A resume skips the script and the commit once the page's commit is on `main`. A replay never reaches this stage. The result's `line` ends with the page's commit and the version that the publish gave.

input.prompt:
You reconstruct one piece of the Fortress revival's process history for its curator, the person in charge. Load the `fortress-repo` skill first, then read `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md` whole. You work in `/home/user/fortress`, on `main`. Read only; write one file (below).

## The problem

`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` holds the project's established facts, one entry per line under a permanent number. On 2026-10-13, between about 18:16 and 20:13 UTC, a consolidation cut it from 195 entries and 257.6K characters (median entry 1,139, 161 entries over 600) to 157 entries and 90.2K characters (median 576, 38 over 600) at commit `b67abe3d2`. A test of decisions taken from the shorter record was run to show that nothing critical was lost. On 2026-10-22 a rewrite for clarity grew it to 223K, and the curator accepted that growth. Since then FACTS has grown to 427K, median 1,198, 299 of 339 entries over 600, although a workflow runs after each batch's landing that was built to keep the record in that consolidated form.

The curator's order of 2026-11-24, cleaned of dictation errors: "We did one consolidation of the record, we shrank it, and then we did a rewrite for clarity, which grew it, and I accepted that growth. ... Go back and find out how did we successfully apply the record consolidation earlier, and what is missing from the workflow that was supposed to be doing this job and is failing. ... The whole purpose of the workflow was to encode that successful practice into something that runs after each landing."

Another worker examines the workflow. **Your part is the successful practice: exactly how the consolidation of 2026-10-13 was done, so that it can be set beside the workflow instruction by instruction.**

## What to find

1. **The method as it ran**, step by step: who did what (the coordinating session, scouts, writers, checkers), in which order, on which chunks, with which briefs. Give the exact words of each instruction that told a writer what an entry keeps, what leaves it, and where the text that leaves goes. If the briefs were Agent prompts and not files, take them from the transcript.
2. **What left the entries.** Of the roughly 167K characters removed, how much went where: to `FACTS-history.md` as provenance; left in the reports that the entries point to; moved to a skill as a rule; merged with another entry; removed as stale or as not a fact. Measure it as far as the commits allow, and say how you measured. Then 12 entries before and after, chosen by a fixed rule that you state, each with its removed sentences marked by where they went.
3. **The form that resulted.** What an entry held after the consolidation, part by part (title, the fact, its conditions, what it means for the work, tests named, citations by file and line, pointers to rows, to other entries and to reports), with counts per entry. The evidence file `entry-anatomy.md` (below) has the anatomy at `b67abe3d2`.
4. **The limits that the writers worked under**: any target, budget or cap on an entry's or a chunk's length, in its exact words (the rule's draft speaks of "a chunk's total stays under 600 characters times its entries"), who checked it, and what happened to an entry that went over.
5. **What the curator saw and said**: the pilot or page that he read, his comments on length, register and what belongs in the history, and how each comment changed the method.
6. **The check that nothing was lost**: the record test under `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-test/` (its README, questions, key, grades): what it tested, on which record, and its result.

8. **Which parts of this method were written down for later use**, and where: in `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md` ("The pass", "A consolidation", "The consolidation tools"), in the tools' READMEs, in the workflow's design note `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-landing-workflow.md`. For each step of point 1: is it in a rule or a tool today, in which words, or nowhere?

## Sources

- The rule's design and the consolidation's own notes: `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md` (117K; its sections "The size", "Worked examples" and the items on length), `facts-slice-1.md` to `facts-slice-7.md`, `record-test/`, `record-store-design.md`, `record-store-review.md`, `record-origins-evidence.md`.

Its six files: `entries.md` (each entry that the batch added or changed, its lines at the base and now, its history blocks with who wrote each, and the report sections that it cites); `rows.md` (each row that the batch opened, closed, rewrote or noted); `cites.md` (each other entry, queue item and INDEX line that names a changed entry or row); `plan.md` (PLAN's headings, the lines that the batch added, the other lines that name a changed entry or row, and the lines that look stale: a line whose own review-queue item is settled, a list of items that disagrees with the queue, a review finding that a later commit names); `checks.md` (the record's checks at the worktree's head); `sources.md` (the queries that print the review's routing part, its findings and its part for the curator, and the batch record's items for the curator and what it left for the coordinator). - **C-number**: C1, C2 and so on. The writers, the checker and the judge name the change by it.
- **home**: one of nine. A FACTS entry (F-N); a POSITIONS entry (P-N); an entry's history only (a noted block, when the entry stays and its history lacks a fact); a gap-ledger row (row N); a PLAN line (PLAN.md:N, with its heading); a PLAN line moved to PLAN-history; a review-queue item (new, or item N); an INDEX line; a line of another note (PATH:N). ## The method

1. Draft the outline first, with a home for every rule that moves.
2. Have the writer write each part whole, by the seven principles of `explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md`. A rewrite is never longer than the text that it replaces.
3. Run a cold read. Review its flags, and have the writer fix them. Only then have a worker put a change that waits for the curator's yes on the page of skill drafts (step 4).
4. Land the change after its cold read, unless it waits for the curator's yes (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions"). Put a change that waits under "Proposed changes" on the page of skill drafts: one item for each section that it rewrites, a whole part included, each with its new text whole, in the form of `SKILL.md`, "Pages".
5. Brief each comment of the curator to the writer, rather than rewrite it yourself. A comment marks a problem area: the writer fixes its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind.
6. Settle the writer's minor decisions from the record. `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", says which changes wait for the curator, and how a new rule is named.
7. After each change to the coordinator skill or to `fortress-repo` lands, have a worker update that skill's page: the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill, the page of `fortress-repo` changes for `fortress-repo`. The boot note holds both links. Give the worker the page's URL, and have it publish by that URL. The record-landing workflow runs this update itself for the changes to `fortress-repo` that follow a landing (`references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4). The page of skill drafts has two sections, and the page of `fortress-repo` changes has only the first:
   - Landed changes: only the landed changes that the curator has not read, so that no change lands unseen while the curator is away. The items stand oldest first, numbered on from the page's last item, so every item that the curator finds there is new:
     - If the curator says, on the page or in chat, that they have read the page up to an item, the next update removes that item and every older item. Before each update, the worker reads every comment thread on the page, sent to Claude or not. A comment on a landed item that only says that the curator read it, such as "LGTM", is such a word, at the comment's time; write the newest such word and its time in the boot note's "Pages" line of that page. Every other comment, a yes on a draft among them, drops no item, and the worker quotes it to you. The page worker and the record-landing workflow's page stage both read it there. You may have the update made at once, without waiting for the next landing.
     - A draft is an item under "Proposed changes" that waits for the curator's yes. Its landing, the commit of the approved words, gets no item, unless it fixed a hit of the skills' lint, `explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py`, or a wrong path or section name: then one item shows the fix alone. The skill writer first runs the lint and checks the draft's paths and section names; the fix needs no second cold read. Any other change is a change of its own and goes the way its kind goes.
     - Every other item stays until the curator says, on the page or in chat, that they have read it.
     - A folded item is an item into which a later change was folded (`SKILL.md`, "Pages"). It strikes through the text before its first change, marks every word added since, and lists each change's reason in order.
     - The curator's word that they read the page up to an item drops a folded item only if the fold was published before the word's time. Otherwise the item stays, with the fold marked.
     - If a change touches the passages of two items that the curator has not said they read, fold it into each. Its part outside them gets its own item.
     - The one item that a draft's landing fix gets is folded too, if its passage has an item that the curator has not said they read.

     The item takes the form of a landed item in `SKILL.md`, "Pages". It shows the change against the skill's text before it, or, for an approved draft whose words changed at the landing, against the approved words. It gives the change's reason, which may come from a cold read, a hit of the skills' lint, a fix at a draft's landing, or the record entry that the orientation workflow, in update mode, took in. The reason says in plain words what was wrong and what the text now says. It never cites a cold read's flag by its code or number, a judge's ruling by its number, or an item of a task by its number.
   - Proposed changes: the items that wait for the curator's yes. When an approved item lands, a worker takes it off this section.

- Run `skill-writer.sh new <task-file>` for a fresh writer, and `skill-writer.sh resume <task-file>` for its next task, within the hour. Start a fresh writer after a pass over a whole skill, or after your compaction.
- The writer edits and commits the skill files. You push, except inside the record-landing workflow, which pushes the writer's commits itself.
- If a part that the curator approved is written again, have a Fable reviewer compare the two. Where it finds a regression, it writes a synthesis of both, never a wholesale revert.
- After a rule enters a skill from the curator's words, check that the skill caught the meaning, by a cold read or a test.
- If a practice that a skill states is in question, have a Sonnet scout check what the workers actually did. If they found a better way, write that way into the skill.
- Keep batch structure out of `fortress-repo`. The workflow or the brief sets which roles exist, and who builds, checks, commits and pushes.
- After each landing, the orientation workflow updates `fortress-repo`'s `references/revival-changes.md` (`references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4). `fortress-repo`'s `SKILL.md` keeps only what does not change from batch to batch.

skill-writer.sh
skills-lint.py
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts or resumes the skill writer: a headless Claude session that edits the
# project skills. A headless session writes its prompt cache with the one-hour
# life, where an Agent-tool subagent gets five minutes, so a writer resumed
# within the hour reads its context from the cache.
#
# Usage:
#   skill-writer.sh new <task-file>     a fresh writer: the standing brief
#                                       (../skill-writer-brief.md), then the task
#   skill-writer.sh resume <task-file>  the task, sent to the current writer
#
# The session id and each task's JSON output are kept under the repository's
# tmp/skill-writer/, which is ignored, or under SKILL_WRITER_STATE if it is set:
# the record-landing workflow keeps its writer there, so that its run leaves the
# coordinator's writer session as it was. The script prints the writer's report,
# its session id and the tokens the task wrote to the cache.
set -euo pipefail
. "$(dirname "$0")/tiers.sh"
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)
state="${SKILL_WRITER_STATE:-$repo/tmp/skill-writer}"
mkdir -p "$state"
mode=${1:?new or resume}
task=$(cd "$(dirname "${2:?task file}")" && pwd)/$(basename "$2")
tools=(Read Edit Write Glob Grep
       "Bash(git add:*)" "Bash(git commit:*)" "Bash(git diff:*)" "Bash(git log:*)"
       "Bash(git status:*)" "Bash(git show:*)" "Bash(git grep:*)" "Bash(wc:*)"
       "Bash(explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh:*)"
       "Bash(python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py:*)")
out="$state/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$mode.json"
cd "$repo"
case $mode in
  new)
    id=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')
    echo "$id" > "$state/session"
    { cat explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md
      printf '\n# Your first task\n\n'
      cat "$task"; } |
      claude -p --model "$WRITER_MODEL" ${WRITER_EFFORT:+--effort "$WRITER_EFFORT"} --session-id "$id" --permission-mode acceptEdits \
        --allowedTools "${tools[@]}" --output-format json > "$out" ;;
  resume)

content.text:
Both answers are in now. The second worker reconstructed how the October consolidation cut FACTS from 258K to 90K.

**What made October work:**
- **The writers' brief said: "Your default is to cut.** A check that nothing is lost is not your goal; the history file and the reports already keep everything."
- **A hard size limit per chunk:** "the chunk's total is under 600 characters times its staying entries". Every writer treated it as a cap. It did 83% of the cutting.
- **Each cut had to name where the text lives.** Most of what left was detail that belongs in the reports: file-and-line citations, test lists and measurements were 64% of it.
- **A test of decisions** on the shortened record: 29 of 30 on the pilot, 30 of 30 at the end.
- **You read old and new texts on a page first** and commented.

**What went wrong:** none of the first four was ever written into a rule or a tool. The skill's section on consolidation was written the same evening and left them out. It kept only "near 600 characters, a check, not a cap". The landing workflow was then built on the clarity rewrite's method, whose brief says "Clarity comes first" and sets no limit. On 11-02 the skill handed consolidation to that workflow, which by its own design does not do it.

Reconstruction: https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-11-24-record-regrowth/evidence/consolidation-of-october.md

That link works once I push, which waits a few minutes for the skill change below.

The skill change on the boot note is written and is in its cold read now. The new rule's words:

> "When the curator asks if you can be compacted, and when the session ends or hands on its work, rewrite the boot note whole, commit and push it, then answer. Between those points, write in it only what a part names for a launch or a page. Your context survives a process stop, but not a compaction."

When the cold read's flags are fixed, I'll push and tell you. Then you can compact, and I'll bring the fix for the workflow and the plan to compress FACTS in the fresh context.
